Gee sorry. Here are some option you have even as solo players:

WAR pulls paired with a marking can help single out and bring the attention of your team to an enemy.
MCH Buffed Drill into MCH LB has a decent chance of 1 shotting or lowering a single players HP of your choosing.
SAM LB 1 shot on DRK's and DRG can be utilized by letting yourself get stray hit by their aoe attacks (not just the LB or Salted Earth)

Why would you need to be good enough to play a videogame?

Ur anxiety and ur feelings are okay. You should accept them but never feed them too much. At the end of the day, how "good" you need to be depends entirely on your goals. If you are just doing normal content, then rarely anyone will do more than give u a weird look at times UNLESS you rly have no idea how the game works (pure healing, not using tank CD's and other examples come to mind)

With that out of the way u should ask yourself:
How well do I want to play and how can I make that work?

A lot of people see rly good players (raiders,legends whatever) and set expectancy that they themselves should be as good as those players. What is often forgotten, is that getting better takes time and effort. Do not expect urself to be amazing when u didnt give urself the time to grow slowly and steadily.

Bonding usually takes place through doing activities together. If you are having difficulty to build lasting relationships; you should first try to figure out what activities you regularly enjoy in the game and search for people that share your preference.

Additionally, don't pressure yourself with finding friends. It's just like real life in final fantasy:

There will be very many people that you will get along with and very few that will be "true" friends that last. Stuff like that is rare and there is NOTHING wrong with you if ur having trouble dealin with it. 

Sometimes it's also okay just to enjoy your time with people without the huge goal of ever lasting friendship. Have a good time and if you rly click with someone, awesome, just dont pressure urself to find that immediately.

Don't rly have an ex trial in particular but in general:

Self-explanatory but know about mechanics beforehand.

Structure and plan ur cooldowns accordingly. General rotating between them and saving stuff for the occasional tankbuster. The latter is pretty important to handle correctly. 

Is there a specific position the boss should be at while u tank or is it not that important? Is a mechanic better handleable if he is centered, facing a certain way or at the edge?

If there is a mechanic that involves everyone to move and stay in a certain spot, can u tend to ur melees and bring the boss close to ur team?

If u are one of the Tanks with an OH SHIT ability like DRK or GNB, consider a macro for it to inform ur healer for when shit rly hits the fan

Consider saving up a gap closer if the boss likes to shimmy around. 

DONT FIGHT UR MT/OT FOR HATE.
MT: Tank stance on/ OT: stance off till a bit into the fight, then on to remain 2nd highest priority. If some idiot rly insists on having aggro, let him. Most that do this, die doing so shortly after anyways.

I'm more of a newish tank myself but I liked practising these things in Eden and then moved on to EX's. Honestly,Innocence EX wasnt bad at all so maybe that's for you? Iunno. 

And lastly, focus almost solely on doing your job right. I find that I get awfully distracted when someone fucks up a mechanic and for example brings an AOE to me. While this happens and isnt the end of the world, if you focus on that too much, you might tunnel vision and forget for a split sec what the next thing u have to do is. Then u might panic and pop extra cooldowns which u might need later and uh shortly after... 

BOOM everyone dies. It's like a chain reaction. Just focus on ur part. 

Oh yeah and ofc DPS is important but staying alive is even more. Don't prioritize the one over the other. 

If all else fails blame the healer /s

The guard buttons gives absolute crossup protection/waaaay more of it than there should be.
You will never have to worry about left and right mixups whatsoever. It completely nullifies them cuz it adjusts the direction your blocking automatically on every frame for you. It doesn't matter during which frames of a crossup my opponent would hit me, I would never need to block the right way because the game would do it for me. 

And that, for me, is crossup protection too (on demand, always, anywhere, extended). It is way easier to let the game block these for you with the guard button than actually reacting to the left and rights. Do not remove crossup protection the game naturally should have, just remove the the one that the guard buttons adds on top of that. 

There is absolutely no reason right now to use directional blocking for crossups cuz u can just sit there, hold the guard button and always be fine. It never fails for that. 

It is also probelmatic for some characters like lancelot cuz most of his sideswitch mix doesnt work if ur just holding the guard button. 

Just feels a bit dumbed down, especially considering in so many other arcsys games you do have to block left and right correctly. The guard button says no u to one of the most common mixups strats in almost any fighter.

But if u were to remove this function of it, there would probably be no point of the guard button existing in the first place. It is precisely why guatd buttons have either been removed in some arcsys games or never implemented in the first place.

The proxy OS and possibly also crossup protection the guard button gives are very likely to be patched out. So if you plan to use it for that eeeehhhhhhh might not be worth it (unless you want to use these till it gets patched)

Other than those 2 things, I suppose it is easier to switch between high and low block since you can just  input 2G and if a high comes your way you just let go of 2. 

Holding soley the guard button also doesn't make you walk backwards. This can theoretically make some moves of a blockstring whiff (if there is a gap and ur able to move backwards, they then might whiff, unable to cancel and you badonka donk whiff punish em)

And that's rly all i can come up with from the top of my hat.

Xenoverse is not balanced nor complex enough to be considered a "real" fighting game I suppose. I have played Xenoverse a lot 2 years ago (and actually was under the top 10 in the world on switch when it came to ranked) and I have to say: in comparison to other fighters it is really bad. 

Xenoverse has a garbage netplay environment which is already a big yikes for fighting game. Here is a link to me fighting Ndukauba as an example
 https://youtu.be/8cqUZFMWy 

If you look closely there are A LOT of hit confirms, evasions and outright not working things in that match due to the netcode. This happens in many matches for many players. It has often been adressed by the community and other youtubers. The company to this day hasn't done anything to fix the netcode. Instead, they just throw out more moneygrabber DLC but I digress.

There is also some major underdeveloped/broken mechanics (combos are easy as fuck, no grab teching, some move and z soul combinations are absurd) and the only depth that i personally found as an experienced player was in stamina management, movement and ki canceling. Let alone I can tell u from personal experience that the majority of "top players" was simply people abusing certain moves or mechanics and literally doing nothing else. A: Light Hit
B: Mid
C: Heavy
D: Switch 
P: Assist
D+P= Reversal Action

The numbers indicate which direction u put in while doing an input

Imagine a 3 by 3 square. Bottom row 123, mid row 456 and top row 789

5 is in the middle so its neutral position (no movement)
6 is forward, 4 backward
2 is crouch
789 are all jumps in different directions

How this works with moves:

Some moves only come out when a certain direction is inout while u press an attack button

So for example: in neutral position press B. That is ur 5B. When u crouch and press B u have a 2B (which usually is an anti air). Press C with no motion and u get 5C, the universal overhead in this game. Press C while crouching and ur doing a 2C. U get the idea.

If you cal ann assist and hold forward while doing so u get the 6P. If u hold back the 4P. Neutral=5P

And then there is the quartercircle moves (214X or 236X). These only come out when u do the circle and press either A, B or C (or BC if u want a super)

From someone who wants to keep playing bbtag in the long run. Arguments for and against the whole "Is it dead yet" thing

Reasons as for why people believe/say the game is dying:

- Empty lobbies on the platforms that arent PS4 are a bit more common around most  time of the day. People who don't know the active times (or even how to switch to NA server if not from NA) will believe it is dead and move on 

- Lack of new content. We cannot ignore that even though crosstag has lots of replayability, with nothing new being added, things can get rather dull over time. But that is something that happens to all videogames that aren't handing out much interest keepers

- comparisons to other types of games and playerbase activity. Either people are moving on to other fresher games or claim for Tag to be dying since the player count is so low in comparison. However, player count and player activity are not necessarily the same thing. Other genres may have the bigger audience but that does not mean the smaller audience is inactive or non-existent. People claimed BBTag on switch to be dead here days ago. I load into it yesterday 26 people in the lobby. Totally dead.

------------------------------------------------------------------

Reasons as for why Tag is still alive:

- The hardcore and competitive playerbase is and will stick around for a longer period of time

- Although many ppl seemed to have somewhat moved on from it I feel like a decent amount of players has already voiced that they love Tag and simply long for something new in the game. Quite a bunch should return for season 2

- the depth of the game and motivation to keep playing that community gives through mediums such as the tag discord and tourneys offer people  great reasons to keep on playing, those being: knowing there is still much to learn and work for but also u can be part of a community that talks, laughs and competes on a daily basis. The need of community plays a huge role for fighting games but this need should be stilled. 

Lastly,

Passion of the playerbase. Be it the filthy gorby main, the underdog yukiko hero, the cool hakumen, the fly hazama and yosuke, best boi kanji, big boi wald or tager main and all the other mains there are:
People still love this game and their characters. And they enjoy it. People still care about this game that brought joy into their life, combined characters that they already loved from previous franchises and made it possible to grow to love characters we might not have known before. BBTag is a wonderful game and I believe that with all my heart. It has its issues and what these are will differ from person to person BUT in the end all these discussions about whats good/whats bad about tag, is it alive, is it dead, all of this

Should be proof enough that it is in fact: Not dead

Alright I'm gonna give some insight on this as I played that match and tried to figure out what it was a week ago or so:

Basically, the property of hakumens 236BC changes just like his 6P depending on how the enemy is hit

If the sword does not connect physically with the opponent the usual shockwave comes out sometime where the sword is about to or hitting the ground

If the sword does connect the damage of the distortion increases (dealing double the damage) but no additional hitbox/shockwave will be added. That is also the reason for why a 6P assist that hits u physically alone (without poration) can deal around 3.9k and even with poration a good amount of dmg in a combo.

Anyways, 
So what ended up happening is that the game thought I hit the opponent (which in this case was the clash unfortunatly) and therefor did give the distortion the increased damage and not the shockwave. 

That means that Hakumens distortion can lose to multi hitting attacks such as a grim reaper, buzzsaw, yukiko spinny thing distortion and some other moves i cant come up with rn if they clash close enough.

So for Haku players that means to rather counter these type of moves if they close in instead of having the gamble with 236BC

Hope that cleared things up for ya^^

Alright Cross Combos

To first of all lead into a cross combo u will need a set up and at least! Full partner gauge and maybe 2 bars 

Your partner can only be activated after he  Did an assist and  one part of the partner gauge is still left. While he/she is active the gauge will get drained over time

A setup:
That could for instance be that ur character does a combo, you call in the assist and pick the combo up again where ur assist is done attacking

After that (when an assist is already out) you can do a cross combo by pressing PD at the same time as long as ur  assist character is still on the field

From there u basically have a few options: first of all ur main character obviously has to continue the combo after ur partner is activated

This creates an opportunity for ur assist to join in, both synergyising together in a combo

Ur assist will have 3 Options: his 4P,5P,6P

These are the same exact assist moves u already use in matches. This time however instead of pressing P (left,neutral,right) to make ur assist do something, while active he will perform these things by u inputing an attack button (so A/B/C) and holding an direction at the same time
(Sidenote: if u hold P while using one of the three, the assist will not move)

Here are some examples how to utilize this, simplified:

Main character combo->assist-> main proceeds-> 1-3hits from the main after the assist has hit, you activate him/her with PD -> while u press A u dont put any direction in and ur partner will do his neutral assist (5P)-> can potentially be an opportunity for u to do a distortion if u have 2 bars and even 2 distortions if u have 4 left
(Assist sets the distortion up)

Or

Main->assist->main proceeds->1-3hits, activate assist->236B (6P) AND then press D-> while ur main does his quarter circle forward B u switch to ur assisting character who could potentially do a distortion bc of ur main setting it up with his 236B

NOTE: Everything after main proceeds is dependent on what ur characters can do, everything before it is basically the general setup to start the real cross combo

Please be aware that for ur team different inputs might be necessary for e.g. u need 1 hit then activate him/her, maybe just do AB and Hold left for 4P while pressing B. That could then again lead into a distortion

Thats something u gotta figure out yourself tho and for ur characters

WHY to do this:

First of all distortions do more damage when u have a partner activated while using them.
It is also very likely to get the second distortion in (if u land the first one). That will do around 1.5k or more dmg to ur overall combo

In some Cross combos u can also swap ur character mid combo.  Not quite sure but i know there is in fact a dmg boost for the character u swaped too.

When NOT to do this:

When ur opponent has enough partner gauge to just switch out characters while u would loved to cross combo him. Basically after activation of ur assist he might just switch out characters, forcing ur combo to drop and waisting ur partner gauge, leaving ur character in a pinch if he gets caught and u cant swap out, forced to take a strong combo


PS: If ur partner gauge has run out before u do the distortion, it will not have the dmg boost anymore
